title: Ewing sarcoma immunopeptidomics
projectDescription: Ewing Sarcoma (EwS) is a rare pediatric malignancy characterized by a unique t(11:22) (q24;q12) translocation resulting in the EWSR1::FLI1 fusion. Recent reports indicate the EWSR1::FLI1 fusion onco-protein drives aberrant expression of numerous transcripts, including Lipoxygenase Homology Domains 1 (LOX¬HD1). Given its highly restricted protein expression pattern and role in EwS tumorigenesis and metastasis, LOXHD1 may serve as a novel immunotherapeutic target in this malignancy. LOXHD1 immunogenic epitopes restricted to HLA-A*02:01 allowed for the isolation of high avidity TCRs.  LOXHD1-specific TCR engineered CD8+ T cells confer cytotoxic activity against a panel of HLA-A*02:01+ EwS tumor cell lines and adoptive transfer leads to tumor eradication in a mouse xenograft model of EwS. This study nominates LOXHD1 as an onco-fusion regulated / non-mutated EwS tumor associated antigen with expression limited to inner hair cells of the cochlea, adult testis, and EwS
sampleProcessingProtocol: HLA-I peptides were extracted from 500 million SK-N-MC/HLA-A*02:01 cells before and after exposure to IFN- (n = 6). In brief, the cells were lysed in a solution containing 0.5% IGEPAL, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, and 150 mM NaCl, supplemented with protease inhibitors (Complete Protease Inhibitor Cocktail Tablet; Roche Molecular Biochemicals) for 45 minutes at 4°C. Subsequently, lysates underwent ultracentrifugation at 40,000 g, and HLA-I complexes were isolated using a two-step antibody-based purification approach. Initially, HLA-A2 antibody (bb7.2) was employed, followed by a pan HLA-I antibody (w6/32) (51). The HLA peptide-bound molecules were then eluted from the affinity column using five column volumes of 10% acetic acid. The eluted HLA-I peptide complexes were loaded onto a monolithic C18 RP-HPLC column (Chromolith Speed Rod; Merck) with a 4.6 mm internal diameter and 50 mm length, operating at a flow rate of 1 ml/min. An EttanLC HPLC system (GE Healthcare) was used for this purpose, with buffer A composed of 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), and peptides were separated by increasing concentrations of buffer B (80% acetonitrile/0.1% TFA). The fractionated peptides were subsequently combined into nine pools and subjected to analysis using an Orbitrap Fusion™ Tribrid™ mass spectrometer (ThermoFisher Scientific).
dataProcessingProtocol: LC-MS/MS Data Acquisition For peptide identification, we employed a Data-Dependent Acquisition (DDA) strategy. Using a Dionex UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano system equipped with a Dionex UltiMate 3000 RS autosampler, the samples were introduced via an Acclaim PepMap 100 trap column (100 µm × 2 cm, nanoViper, C18, 5 µm, 100Å; Thermo Scientific) before being loaded onto an Acclaim PepMap RSLC analytical column (75 µm × 50 cm, nanoViper, C18, 2 µm, 100Å; Thermo Scientific). Peptides were chromatographically separated by a gradient of 80% acetonitrile (ACN) and 0.1% formic acid (FA) at a flow rate of 250 nl/min over a 65-minute period. Subsequently, they were analyzed using an Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific).In each acquisition cycle, a full MS1 scan was conducted (resolution: 70,000; AGC target: 3e6; maximum IT: 120 ms; scan range: 375–1800 m/z). This was followed by up to 12 subsequent MS2 scans (resolution: 17,500; AGC target: 1e5; maximum IT: 120 ms; isolation window: 1.8 m/z; scan range: 200–2,000 m/z; NCE: 27).  HLA Peptide Identification MS/MS spectra were subjected to analysis using PEAKS Studio X software. The MS files were imported into PEAKS X, and the following parameters were configured: a parent mass error tolerance of 10 parts per million (ppm) and a fragmentation mass error of 0.02 Da. An initial de novo search was conducted on all MS/MS spectra against peptide sequences, followed by a search against the human proteome database (Uniprot Human Reviewed Proteins downloaded as of October 2021). Variable modifications were considered, including Oxidation (M), Deamidation (NQ), and Cysteinylation (C) and a false discovery rate (FDR) of 5% at spectra level was implemented.
